partners.diseaseBName: congenital heart defects and ectodermal dysplasia
partners.mechanism_chain: SPTLC1 (HGNC:11030) —DISRUPTS→ Sphingolipid biosynthesis (GO:0006695); Sphingolipid biosynthesis (GO:0006695) —LEADS_TO→ Neuropathy (HP:0000759); PRKD1 (HGNC:9370) —DISRUPTS→ Sphingolipid biosynthesis (GO:0006695); PRKD1 (HGNC:9370) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart defects (HP:0001627); PRKD1 (HGNC:9370) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal dysplasia (HP:0001052). Mutations in SPTLC1 disrupt sphingolipid biosynthesis, leading to neuropathy. PRKD1, while not directly in the core sphingolipid synthesis pathway, has been implicated in downstream signaling and cellular processes that can be affected by altered sphingolipid levels, and its mutations directly cause congenital heart defects and ectodermal dysplasia. This hypothesis posits that both genes, through distinct but converging impacts on cellular homeostasis and potentially downstream signaling pathways influenced by sphingolipids, contribute to distinct disease phenotypes.
